description: Validate any IBAN using the official ISO 13616 mod-97 checksum, with clean grouped formatting.

faqs.a: The first four characters are moved to the end, every letter is replaced by two digits (A=10 … Z=35), and the resulting number must leave remainder 1 when divided by 97.
No. A valid checksum only proves the IBAN is well-formed. It cannot confirm the account exists, is open, or belongs to anyone.
faqs.q: Does a valid IBAN mean the account exists?

faqs.a: No — validation runs entirely in your browser and the IBAN is never stored or sent anywhere.
faqs.q: Is my IBAN sent to a server?

howto: Paste or type the IBAN (spaces are fine).
The format is checked, then the official mod-97 checksum runs.
A green result means the IBAN is structurally valid.
Use the grouped format and country code for copying into bank forms.
title: IBAN Validator
